newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet soon to decide details of KGHM sale.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet soon to decide details of KGHM sale.

text.p: Depending on how much Poland will keep of its KGHM Polska Miedz SA copper concern, the firm's international offer will be placed only in London or both London and New York, a deputy privatisation minister said.

Piotr Czyzewski told reporters at a privatisation seminar that the government would soon approve a privatisation plan for KGHM, deciding on the size of the treasury stake after the sell-off and other details.

"A substantial stake will remain in the hands of the state treasury while the remaining shares will be divided between the domestic offer for institutions and retail investors and the international offer," he said.

"If the stake (to be retained by the state) is smaller, KGHM shares will be offered in London and New York. If, however, the state retains more shares, we envisage a share offer just in London," Czyzewski said.
Czyzewski would not elaborate on the size of stakes that were being considered.

Earlier the ministry had signalled it wanted to float 15 percent of KGHM in London and another 10 percent of shares on the Warsaw bourse but further details were to be determined by privatisation advisers and approved by the government.
